claim:
Let \(\mathcal M=(M,\in)\) be a transitive set model of \(\mathrm{ZF}\), and let \(I
e\varnothing\). On the classical direct power \(M^I\), define \(f\in^*g\iff orall i\in I,\ f(i)\in g(i)\). Every equivalence relation compatible with \(\in^*\) is equality: if \(f
e g\), the coordinatewise singleton function \(s_f(i)=\{f(i)\}\) satisfies \(f\in^*s_f\) but \(g
otin^*s_f\). Consequently, when \(|I|\ge2\), the direct power's failure of extensionality cannot be repaired by any quotient that induces a well-defined membership relation.

correctness.rationale: For any distinct \(f\) and \(g\), choose a coordinate where their values differ and form the coordinatewise singleton \(s_f\). Then \(f\in^*s_f\) but \(g\notin^*s_f\), contradicting compatibility of any congruence that identifies \(f\) and \(g\). Pairing in the ground model guarantees \(s_f\) belongs to the function domain. A separate two-coordinate witness proves extensionality failure when \(|I|\ge2\).

originality.rationale: The primary recent preprint establishes a single extensionality counterexample for the direct power. The present claim proves that every membership-compatible congruence is equality for any nonempty index set, yielding a no-quotient-repair theorem when there are at least two coordinates.
residual_risks: The older Weinstein thesis was not available in full text; it could contain a related observation not indexed by the searched terminology.
The proof is short and derives from the coordinatewise singleton construction; priority for an equivalent observation outside the inspected sources is not ruled out.
The result does not address alternative quotient constructions that change the semantics or the membership relation.

value.rationale: The result answers a concrete semantic repair question raised by the primary preprint’s discussion of intensional identity. It proves that no nontrivial quotient can preserve the classical direct-power membership relation; therefore the extensionality defect cannot be fixed by identifying elements while keeping membership well-defined. This sharply limits the quotient-based route without ruling out the paper’s alternative Boolean-valued semantics.
